Muscle lactate production increases when glycolytic flux outpaces mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation and lactate clearance, as in intense exercise, ischemia/hypoxia, or impaired mitochondrial function. Neither "pyruvate cannot be formed from glucose breakdown" nor "oxygen is readily available" is correct—readily available oxygen actually favors pyruvate oxidation and reduces lactate production. The best fit is the scenario where oxygen is limited or glycolytic flux exceeds oxidative capacity, not the listed options as worded.

CONFIDENCE: 85
